sanskrit: prabhāvaṃ pauruṣaṃ buddhiṃ jijñāsantyā mayā tava ullapantyā samāśvāsaṃ balavān iva durbalam
english: Wishing to test your power, your manliness, and your intellect, I was encouraging you with words of comfort, as a strong man encourages the weak.

sanskrit: yady etat saṃvijānāsi yadi samyag bravīmy aham kṛtvāsaumyam ivātmānaṃ jayāyottiṣṭha saṃjaya
english: If you recognise this truth, if what I say is right, then make your spirit resolute and rise for victory, O Sañjaya.

sanskrit: asti naḥ kośanicayo mahān aviditas tava tam ahaṃ veda nānyas tam upasaṃpādayāmi te
english: There is a great accumulation of treasure that you do not know of; I know it, and no one else does — I shall make it available to you.

sanskrit: santi naikaśatā bhūyaḥ suhṛdas tava saṃjaya sukhaduḥkhasahā vīra śatārhā anivartinaḥ
english: You have many hundreds of friends, O Sañjaya, companions in joy and sorrow, heroes worthy of a hundred, who never turn back in battle.

sanskrit: tādṛśā hi sahāyā vai puruṣasya bubhūṣataḥ īṣad ujjihataḥ kiṃ cit sacivāḥ śatrukarśanāḥ
english: Such are the allies that befit a man who desires greatness — counsellors who crush enemies and who need only a small effort to be roused.

sanskrit: putra uvāca kasya tv īdṛśakaṃ vākyaṃ śrutvāpi svalpacetasaḥ tamo na vyapahanyeta sucitrārthapadākṣaram
english: The son said: Whose darkness of mind would not be dispelled upon hearing such words — words whose syllables and meaning are so wonderfully varied — even if his understanding were small?

sanskrit: udake dhūr iyaṃ dhāryā sartavyaṃ pravaṇe mayā yasya me bhavatī netrī bhaviṣyad bhūtadarśinī
english: This burden must be borne upon the water; I must now move swiftly down the slope — for you, who see things as they truly are, shall be my guide.

sanskrit: ahaṃ hi vacanaṃ tvattaḥ śuśrūṣur aparāparam kiṃ cit kiṃ cit prativadaṃs tūṣṇīm āsaṃ muhur muhuḥ
english: Indeed, eager to hear word after word from you, replying with a word here and a word there, I fell silent again and again.

sanskrit: atṛpyann amṛtasyeva kṛcchrāl labdhasya bāndhavāt udyacchāmy eṣa śatrūṇāṃ niyamāya jayāya ca
english: Like one not satiated by nectar obtained with difficulty from a kinsman, I rise now to the subduing of enemies and to victory.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca sadaśva iva sa kṣiptaḥ praṇunno vākyasāyakaiḥ tac cakāra tathā sarvaṃ yathāvad anuśāsanam
english: Kuntī said: Urged on and spurred like a noble horse by the arrows of her words, he did everything just as she had instructed.

sanskrit: idam uddharṣaṇaṃ bhīmaṃ tejovardhanam uttamam rājānaṃ śrāvayen mantrī sīdantaṃ śatrupīḍitam
english: A counsellor should recite this formidable and excellent exhortation — which augments heroic energy — to a king who is sinking, oppressed by enemies.

sanskrit: jayo nāmetihāso 'yaṃ śrotavyo vijigīṣuṇā mahīṃ vijayate kṣipraṃ śrutvā śatrūṃś ca mardati
english: This is the history called Jaya and it should be heard by one who desires conquest; upon hearing it he swiftly conquers the earth and crushes his enemies.

sanskrit: idaṃ puṃsavanaṃ caiva vīrājananam eva ca abhīkṣṇaṃ garbhiṇī śrutvā dhruvaṃ vīraṃ prajāyate
english: This is both a rite for the generation of a male child and a generator of heroes; if a pregnant woman hears it repeatedly she will certainly give birth to a hero.

sanskrit: vidyāśūraṃ tapaḥśūraṃ damaśūraṃ tapasvinam brāhmyā śriyā dīpyamānaṃ sādhuvādena saṃmatam
english: Heroic in learning, heroic in austerity, heroic in self-restraint, an ascetic blazing with the glory of Brahman, honoured with praise by the righteous —

sanskrit: arciṣmantaṃ balopetaṃ mahābhāgaṃ mahāratham dhṛṣṭavantam anādhṛṣyaṃ jetāram aparājitam
english: Radiant, endowed with strength, of great fortune, a great chariot-warrior, bold yet unapproachable, a victor never defeated —

sanskrit: niyantāram asādhūnāṃ goptāraṃ dharmacāriṇām tadarthaṃ kṣatriyā sūte vīraṃ satyaparākramam
english: A restrainer of the wicked, a protector of the righteous — it is for this purpose that a kṣatriya woman gives birth to a hero of true valour.

sanskrit: kunty uvāca arjunaṃ keśava brūyās tvayi jāte sma sūtake upopaviṣṭā nārībhir āśrame parivāritā
english: Kuntī said: Tell Arjuna, O Keśava, that at the time of his birth, when I was sitting in my lying-in chamber surrounded by women in the hermitage —

sanskrit: athāntarikṣe vāg āsīd divyarūpā manoramā sahasrākṣasamaḥ kunti bhaviṣyaty eṣa te sutaḥ
english: — a divine, beautiful, enchanting voice arose in the sky: 'O Kuntī, this son of yours shall be equal to the Thousand-Eyed One.

sanskrit: eṣa jeṣyati saṃgrāme kurūn sarvān samāgatān bhīmasenadvitīyaś ca lokam udvartayiṣyati
english: He shall conquer in battle all the Kurus assembled together, and together with Bhīmasena as his second, he will overturn the world.

sanskrit: putras te pṛthivīṃ jetā yaśaś cāsya divaspṛśam hatvā kurūn grāmajanye vāsudevasahāyavān
english: Your son shall conquer the earth and his fame shall touch the sky; slaying the Kurus in the great battle, he will have Vāsudeva as his ally.

sanskrit: pitryam aṃśaṃ pranaṣṭaṃ ca punar apy uddhariṣyati bhrātṛbhiḥ sahitaḥ śrīmāṃs trīn medhān āhariṣyati
english: He shall recover the paternal inheritance that has been lost, and together with his brothers, in his splendour, he will perform three great sacrifices.'

sanskrit: taṃ satyasaṃdhaṃ bībhatsuṃ savyasācinam acyuta yathāham evaṃ jānāmi balavantaṃ durāsadam tathā tad astu dāśārha yathā vāg abhyabhāṣata
english: O Acyuta, I know that Bībhatsu, the left-handed archer, that man of true pledges, is mighty and difficult to assail — may it be so, O Dāśārha, as the voice declared.

sanskrit: dharmaś ced asti vārṣṇeya tathā satyaṃ bhaviṣyati tvaṃ cāpi tat tathā kṛṣṇa sarvaṃ saṃpādayiṣyasi
english: If dharma exists, O Vārṣṇeya, truth shall be fulfilled; and you too, O Kṛṣṇa, shall bring all of it to accomplishment.

sanskrit: nāhaṃ tad abhyasūyāmi yathā vāg abhyabhāṣata namo dharmāya mahate dharmo dhārayati prajāḥ
english: I do not begrudge what the voice declared; homage to the great dharma — it is dharma that sustains all living beings.

sanskrit: etad dhanaṃjayo vācyo nityodyukto vṛkodaraḥ yadarthaṃ kṣatriyā sūte tasya kālo 'yam āgataḥ na hi vairaṃ samāsādya sīdanti puruṣarṣabhāḥ
english: Tell Dhanañjaya and the ever-ready Vṛkodara that the time has come for that purpose for which a kṣatriya woman gives birth — for bulls among men do not falter when they encounter enmity.

sanskrit: viditā te sadā buddhir bhīmasya na sa śāmyati yāvadantaṃ na kurute śatrūṇāṃ śatrukarśanaḥ
english: You have always known Bhīma's disposition — that chastiser of enemies will not rest until he brings the enemies to their final end.

sanskrit: sarvadharmaviśeṣajñāṃ snuṣāṃ pāṇḍor mahātmanaḥ brūyā mādhava kalyāṇīṃ kṛṣṇāṃ kṛṣṇa yaśasvinīm
english: O Mādhava, please speak to the auspicious, illustrious Kṛṣṇā — the daughter-in-law of the great-souled Pāṇḍu, who is versed in all the distinctions of dharma.

sanskrit: yuktam etan mahābhāge kule jāte yaśasvini yan me putreṣu sarveṣu yathāvat tvam avartithāḥ
english: This is fitting, O greatly fortunate one born in a noble lineage, O illustrious one — that you have conducted yourself rightly toward all my sons.

sanskrit: mādrīputrau ca vaktavyau kṣatradharmaratāv ubhau vikrameṇārjitān bhogān vṛṇītaṃ jīvitād api
english: And say to the two sons of Mādrī, who are both devoted to the kṣatriya dharma: 'Choose the enjoyments won by valour, even at the cost of life itself.'

sanskrit: vikramādhigatā hy arthāḥ kṣatradharmeṇa jīvataḥ mano manuṣyasya sadā prīṇanti puruṣottama
english: For the riches obtained through valour by one who lives according to the kṣatriya dharma always delight the heart of a man, O best of men.

sanskrit: yac ca vaḥ prekṣamāṇānāṃ sarvadharmopacāyinī pāñcālī paruṣāṇy uktā ko nu tat kṣantum arhati
english: And as for Pāñcālī — she who enhances all dharma — while you all looked on she was spoken to with harsh words; who could bear that?

sanskrit: na rājyaharaṇaṃ duḥkhaṃ dyūte cāpi parājayaḥ pravrājanaṃ sutānāṃ vā na me tad duḥkhakāraṇam
english: The seizure of the kingdom does not grieve me, nor does defeat at dice, nor the exile of my sons — none of these is the cause of my suffering.

sanskrit: yat tu sā bṛhatī śyāmā sabhāyāṃ rudatī tadā aśrauṣīt paruṣā vācas tan me duḥkhataraṃ matam
english: But that she — tall and dark — weeping in the assembly, heard those harsh words at that time — that, I consider, is a greater sorrow to me.

sanskrit: strīdharmiṇī varārohā kṣatradharmaratā sadā nādhyagacchat tadā nāthaṃ kṛṣṇā nāthavatī satī
english: Though devoted to a woman's duty, beautiful of form, always engaged in the kṣatriya dharma, Kṛṣṇā could find no protector then — she who has protectors and is a virtuous wife.

sanskrit: taṃ vai brūhi mahābāho sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam arjunaṃ puruṣavyāghraṃ draupadyāḥ padavīṃ cara
english: Tell him — O mighty-armed one, tell Arjuna, that tiger among men, the foremost of all who bear weapons — to follow the path of Draupadī.

sanskrit: viditau hi tavātyantaṃ kruddhāv iva yamāntakau bhīmārjunau nayetāṃ hi devān api parāṃ gatim
english: For you know them well — Bhīma and Arjuna, like death and the Ender when enraged; they could bring even the gods to their final end.

sanskrit: tayoś caitad avajñānaṃ yat sā kṛṣṇā sabhāgatā duḥśāsanaś ca yad bhīmaṃ kaṭukāny abhyabhāṣata paśyatāṃ kuruvīrāṇāṃ tac ca saṃsmārayeḥ punaḥ
english: This was the insult to those two — that Kṛṣṇā was dragged into the assembly, and that Duḥśāsana spoke harsh words to Bhīma while the Kuru heroes looked on — remind them of that again.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavān kuśalaṃ pṛccheḥ saputrān kṛṣṇayā saha māṃ ca kuśalinīṃ brūyās teṣu bhūyo janārdana ariṣṭaṃ gaccha panthānaṃ putrān me paripālaya
english: Ask the Pāṇḍavas of their welfare, along with their sons and with Kṛṣṇā; and tell them I am well, O Janārdana. More than all else, travel a safe road and protect my sons.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca abhivādyātha tāṃ kṛṣṇaḥ kṛtvā cābhipradakṣiṇam niścakrāma mahābāhuḥ siṃhakhelagatis tataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Kṛṣṇa paid his respects to her and circumambulated her, and the mighty-armed one departed from there with the gait of a lion at play.

sanskrit: tato visarjayām āsa bhīṣmādīn kurupuṃgavān āropya ca rathe karṇaṃ prāyāt sātyakinā saha
english: Then he took leave of Bhīṣma and the other foremost Kurus, and having taken Karṇa up onto his chariot, he departed together with Sātyaki.

sanskrit: tataḥ prayāte dāśārhe kuravaḥ saṃgatā mithaḥ jajalpur mahad āścaryaṃ keśave paramādbhutam
english: When the Dāśārha departed, the Kurus gathered together and spoke among themselves about the great and most wondrous marvel that was Keśava.

sanskrit: pramūḍhā pṛthivī sarvā mṛtyupāśasitā kṛtā duryodhanasya bāliśyān naitad astīti cābruvan
english: The whole earth, bound in the noose of death, was bewildered; and because of Duryodhana's foolishness they said: 'This cannot be.'

sanskrit: tato niryāya nagarāt prayayau puruṣottamaḥ mantrayām āsa ca tadā karṇena suciraṃ saha
english: Then the best of men went forth from the city and conversed for a long time with Karṇa.

sanskrit: visarjayitvā rādheyaṃ sarvayādavanandanaḥ tato javena mahatā tūrṇam aśvān acodayat
english: Having taken leave of the son of Rādhā, that joy of all the Yādavas then urged his horses forward with great and swift speed.

sanskrit: te pibanta ivākāśaṃ dārukeṇa pracoditāḥ hayā jagmur mahāvegā manomārutaraṃhasaḥ
english: Urged on by Dāruka, those horses of great speed went as if drinking the sky, swift as thought and wind.

sanskrit: te vyatītya tam adhvānaṃ kṣipraṃ śyenā ivāśugāḥ uccaiḥ sūryam upaplavyaṃ śārṅgadhanvānam āvahan
english: Swiftly crossing that road like swift-moving hawks, they brought the bearer of the Śārṅga bow to Upaplavya before the sun had risen high.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca kuntyās tu vacanaṃ śrutvā bhīṣmadroṇau mahārathau duryodhanam idaṃ vākyam ūcatuḥ śāsanātigam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard Kuntī's words, the two great chariot-warriors Bhīṣma and Droṇa spoke this speech to Duryodhana, who transgresses all authority.

sanskrit: śrutaṃ te puruṣavyāghra kuntyāḥ kṛṣṇasya saṃnidhau vākyam arthavad avyagram uktaṃ dharmyam anuttamam
english: You have heard, O tiger among men, the weighty, composed, righteous, and incomparable words that Kuntī spoke in the presence of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: tat kariṣyanti kaunteyā vāsudevasya saṃmatam na hi te jātu śāmyerann ṛte rājyena kaurava
english: The sons of Kuntī will do what is approved by Vāsudeva; they will never rest, O Kaurava, unless they receive the kingdom.

sanskrit: kleśitā hi tvayā pārthā dharmapāśasitās tadā sabhāyāṃ draupadī caiva taiś ca tan marṣitaṃ tava
english: The Pārthas were oppressed by you, bound in the noose of dharma at that time, and Draupadī too — and all of that was endured from you by them.

sanskrit: kṛtāstraṃ hy arjunaṃ prāpya bhīmaṃ ca kṛtaniśramam gāṇḍīvaṃ ceṣudhī caiva rathaṃ ca dhvajam eva ca sahāyaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca na kṣaṃsyati yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: For having Arjuna who is accomplished in weapons, and Bhīma who is practised in effort, and the Gāṇḍīva bow and two quivers, and the chariot and the standard, and Vāsudeva as ally — Yudhiṣṭhira will no longer endure it.

sanskrit: pratyakṣaṃ te mahābāho yathā pārthena dhīmatā virāṭanagare pūrvaṃ sarve sma yudhi nirjitāḥ
english: It is before your eyes, O mighty-armed one, how the wise Pārtha formerly conquered us all in battle at the city of Virāṭa.

sanskrit: dānavān ghorakarmāṇo nivātakavacān yudhi raudram astraṃ samādhāya dagdhavān astravahninā
english: The Dānavas of terrible deeds — the Nivātakavacas — he burned in battle, drawing the fearful Raudra weapon and incinerating them with the fire of his missiles.

sanskrit: karṇaprabhṛtayaś ceme tvaṃ cāpi kavacī rathī mokṣitā ghoṣayātrāyāṃ paryāptaṃ tan nidarśanam
english: And these men headed by Karṇa, and you yourself — armoured and mounted on your chariot — were all released by him during the cattle-raid excursion. That example alone is sufficient.

sanskrit: praśāmya bharataśreṣṭha bhrātṛbhiḥ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ rakṣemāṃ pṛthivīṃ sarvāṃ mṛtyor daṃṣṭrāntaraṃ gatām
english: Make peace, O foremost of the Bhāratas, with the Pāṇḍava brothers, and let us protect this whole earth which has entered the jaws of death.

sanskrit: jyeṣṭho bhrātā dharmaśīlo vatsalaḥ ślakṣṇavāk śuciḥ taṃ gaccha puruṣavyāghraṃ vyapanīyeha kilbiṣam
english: The eldest brother is righteous in conduct, affectionate, gentle of speech, and pure; go to him, that tiger among men, and remove the sin from here.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭaś cet tvaṃ pāṇḍavena vyapanītaśarāsanaḥ prasannabhrukuṭiḥ śrīmān kṛtā śāntiḥ kulasya naḥ
english: If you are seen by the Pāṇḍava with your bow laid aside, your brow unclouded and serene, O splendid one, then peace will have been made for our lineage.

sanskrit: tam abhyetya sahāmātyaḥ pariṣvajya nṛpātmajam abhivādaya rājānaṃ yathāpūrvam ariṃdama
english: Approach him accompanied by your ministers, embrace the son of the king, and honour the king as you did before, O subduer of foes.

sanskrit: abhivādayamānaṃ tvāṃ pāṇibhyāṃ bhīmapūrvajaḥ pratigṛhṇātu sauhārdāt kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: May Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, the elder brother of Bhīma, receive you as you offer homage, clasping you with both arms out of friendship.

sanskrit: siṃhaskandhorubāhus tvāṃ vṛttāyatamahābhujaḥ pariṣvajatu bāhubhyāṃ bhīmaḥ praharatāṃ varaḥ
english: May Bhīma — with the shoulders and thighs of a lion, with arms long, round, and mighty — the foremost among those who strike, embrace you with both arms.

sanskrit: siṃhagrīvo guḍākeśas tatas tvāṃ puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ abhivādayatāṃ pārthaḥ kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: And then may Pārtha Dhanañjaya, son of Kuntī, lion-necked and thick-haired, with eyes like lotus petals, pay homage to you.

sanskrit: āśvineyau naravyāghrau rūpeṇāpratimau bhuvi tau ca tvāṃ guruvat premṇā pūjayā pratyudīyatām
english: And may those two sons of the Aśvins, tigers among men, matchless in beauty upon the earth, rise to honour you with affection, as they would a teacher.

sanskrit: muñcantv ānandajāśrūṇi dāśārhapramukhā nṛpāḥ saṃgaccha bhrātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ mānaṃ saṃtyajya pārthiva
english: May the kings headed by the Dāśārha shed tears of joy; meet with your brothers, O king, and abandon your pride.

sanskrit: praśādhi pṛthivīṃ kṛtsnāṃ tatas taṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha samāliṅgya ca harṣeṇa nṛpā yāntu parasparam
english: Then rule the entire earth together with those brothers; having embraced one another in joy, may the kings go forth to one another.

sanskrit: alaṃ yuddhena rājendra suhṛdāṃ śṛṇu kāraṇam dhruvaṃ vināśo yuddhe hi kṣatriyāṇāṃ pradṛśyate
english: Enough of war, O king of kings; hear the counsel of your well-wishers — in battle the certain destruction of kṣatriyas is clearly foretold.

sanskrit: jyotīṃṣi pratikūlāni dāruṇā mṛgapakṣiṇaḥ utpātā vividhā vīra dṛśyante kṣatranāśanāḥ
english: Adverse celestial omens, dreadful beasts and birds, and various portents foreboding the destruction of kṣatriyas are being seen, O hero.

sanskrit: viśeṣata ihāsmākaṃ nimittāni vināśane ulkābhir hi pradīptābhir vadhyate pṛtanā tava
english: Especially here among us are signs pointing to destruction; your army shall be slain by blazing meteors.

sanskrit: vāhanāny aprahṛṣṭāni rudantīva viśāṃ pate gṛdhrās te paryupāsante sainyāni ca samantataḥ
english: The draft animals are joyless, weeping as it were, O lord of the people; vultures attend your forces from all sides.

sanskrit: nagaraṃ na yathāpūrvaṃ tathā rājaniveśanam śivāś cāśivanirghoṣā dīptāṃ sevanti vai diśam
english: The city and the royal palace are no longer as they once were; jackals with inauspicious cries hover about the flaming directions.

sanskrit: kuru vākyaṃ pitur mātur asmākaṃ ca hitaiṣiṇām tvayy āyatto mahābāho śamo vyāyāma eva ca
english: Do what your father, your mother, and we your well-wishers say; on you depend both peace and exertion, O mighty-armed one.

sanskrit: na cet kariṣyasi vacaḥ suhṛdām arikarśana tapsyase vāhinīṃ dṛṣṭvā pārthabāṇaprapīḍitām
english: If you do not act on the counsel of your well-wishers, O crusher of enemies, you will burn with anguish when you see your army struck down by Pārtha's arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmasya ca mahānādaṃ nadataḥ śuṣmiṇo raṇe śrutvā smartāsi me vākyaṃ gāṇḍīvasya ca nisvanam yady etad apasavyaṃ te bhaviṣyati vaco mama
english: And hearing the mighty roar of Bhīma bellowing with fiery vigour in battle, and the twang of the Gāṇḍīva — then you will remember my words, if these words of mine prove to have gone against the grain for you.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktas tu vimanās tiryagdṛṣṭir adhomukhaḥ saṃhatya ca bhruvor madhyaṃ na kiṃ cid vyājahāra ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed, he sat dejected, his gaze averted, his face downcast, knitting his brows together, and spoke not a word.

sanskrit: taṃ vai vimanasaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃprekṣyānyonyam antikāt punar evottaraṃ vākyam uktavantau nararṣabhau
english: Seeing him thus dejected, those two bulls among men glanced at each other nearby and once again spoke their reply.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca śuśrūṣum anasūyaṃ ca brahmaṇyaṃ satyasaṃgaram pratiyotsyāmahe pārtham ato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
english: Bhīṣma said: We shall fight against Pārtha — who is eager to learn, free from envy, devoted to the Brahman, and true to his pledges; what could be more painful than this?

sanskrit: droṇa uvāca aśvatthāmni yathā putre bhūyo mama dhanaṃjaye bahumānaḥ paro rājan saṃnatiś ca kapidhvaje
english: Droṇa said: O king, the high esteem and reverence I have for Dhanañjaya — the bearer of the monkey-banner — exceeds even what I have for my own son Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: taṃ cet putrāt priyataraṃ pratiyotsye dhanaṃjayam kṣatradharmam anuṣṭhāya dhig astu kṣatrajīvikām
english: If I must fight against Dhanañjaya, who is dearer to me than my own son, while following the kṣatriya dharma — shame upon the kṣatriya's way of life!

sanskrit: yasya loke samo nāsti kaś cid anyo dhanurdharaḥ matprasādāt sa bībhatsuḥ śreyān anyair dhanurdharaiḥ
english: There is no other archer in the world equal to him; by my grace, that Bībhatsu surpasses all other bearers of the bow.

sanskrit: mitradhrug duṣṭabhāvaś ca nāstiko 'thānṛjuḥ śaṭhaḥ na satsu labhate pūjāṃ yajñe mūrkha ivāgataḥ
english: One who betrays friends, who is malicious, an unbeliever, crooked, and deceitful — he receives no honour among the good, like a fool who arrives at a sacrifice uninvited.

sanskrit: vāryamāṇo 'pi pāpebhyaḥ pāpātmā pāpam icchati codyamāno 'pi pāpena śubhātmā śubham icchati
english: Even when restrained from evil, the evil-souled man desires evil; even when urged toward evil, the pure-souled man desires good.
